sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
The claimants are in appeal being aggrieved by the attribution of 10% negligence on the deceased and also on the ground that the compensation awarded is inadequate.
2. The Tribunal has attributed 10% negligence solely on the ground that the rider of the motor cycle did not possess Driving Licence.

Rathnamma vs R. Govindareddy on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142402148/
2 3.

Having regard to the fact that the chargesheet was laid against the driver of the offending vehicle i.e., the bus, it was inappropriate on the part of the Tribunal to attribute negligence on the deceased.
The finding is, therefore, set aside.

4. The Tribunal has awarded the following sums as compensation :
 Sl.

Particulars Amount  No.
 In (Rs.)
 1. Loss of dependency 6,48,000/-
 2. Loss of consortium and loss of 1,00,000/-
 love and affection
The Tribunal awarded Rs.7,48,000/- as compensation to the claimants and after fixing 10% negligence on the deceased, Tribunal awarded in total Rs.6,73,200/- to the claimants.

6. In order to arrive at the loss of dependency, the Tribunal has determined the monthly income,
notionally at Rs.7,500/-.

As there is no credible evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2018, would be Rs.12,500/-.
7.
Since the deceased was aged 60 years and was self- employed, 10% requires to be added to the monthly income towards future prospects, which would result in the income to be Rs.13,750/-.

If 1/4th is deducted towards personal expenses, his monthly income would be Rs.10,312.5/- and the same is rounded off to Rs.10,300/-.
8.
The income of the deceased for the purposes of determining the 'loss of dependency' would thus be Rs.10,300/-.
9. As the deceased was aged 60 years, a multiplier of '9' would have to be applied.

Consequently, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.11,12,400/- (Rs.10,300/- x 12 x '9') towards 'loss of dependency'.
10.

The claimants being the wife and children, they would each be entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/-
towards 'loss of consortium' i.e., in all Rs.2,20,000/- and they would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- under the 'conventional heads'.

Rathnamma vs R. Govindareddy on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142402148/
3 11.

Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums :
 Sl. Particulars Amount  No.
 In (Rs.)
 1. Loss of dependency 11,12,400/-

2 . Conventional heads 2,20,000/-
 3. Loss of consortium 33,000/-
 Total 13,65,400/-
12.

Thus, the claimant would be entitled for compensation of Rs.13,65,400/- as against Rs.6,73,200/- awarded by the Tribunal, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
13. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
14. On such deposit, the claimants are entitled to withdraw the same as per the terms of the award of the Tribunal.
The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
